title: The induction step in relative dimension one
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism] and smooth of relative dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] with $X$
affine, let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, and let $n$ be an integer
invertible on $S$ with $n\Lambda=0$. Let $q\ge1$. If
$\mathrm{BC}(f,\Lambda,q')$ holds universally for every $q'<q$
([sk-def-bc]), then $\mathrm{BC}(f,\Lambda,q)$ holds universally.

proof.text: Suppose the conclusion fails. By [sk-def-bc] choose a morphism $S_0\to S$ such that the fixed-base property $\mathrm{BC}(f_0,\Lambda,q)$ fails for $f_0:X_0=X\times_SS_0\to S_0$. For every $r\le q-1$ one has $r<q$; the hypothesis implies $\mathrm{BC}(f_0,\Lambda,r)$ universally, since any further base change of $f_0$ is a base change of $f$ along the composite map to $S$. Apply [sk-lem-failure-field] to $f_0$ with these hypotheses and $q\ge1$. It produces an affine scheme $S_1\to S_0$, the base change $f_1:X_1\to S_1$, and a field-valued counterexample to its degree-$q$ base-change map. Write this counterexample as $g_1:\operatorname{Spec}k\to S_1$ with its sheaf $\mathcal F$. Both schemes are affine, so [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine] makes $g_1$ affine, and clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] makes it quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Thus $g_1$ and $\mathcal F$ are among the tests in [sk-def-bc]; their nonisomorphic base-change map proves that $\mathrm{BC}(f_1,\Lambda,q)$ fails at the fixed base $S_1$. This realizes the preliminary affine-base reduction in the blueprint, using its existing field-failure lemma instead of an implicit localization claim.

source.place: Statement used for affine preliminary failure; Stacks Tag 0F07, etale-cohomology.tex, lemma-base-change-does-not-hold-pre. Admissibility of the field-valued test: morphisms.tex, Tag 01SH (lemma-morphism-affines-affine) and Tag 01S7 (lemma-affine-separated).

proof.text: The two successive Cartesian squares identify $f_1$ with the base change of $f$ along $S_1\to S_0\to S$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] makes $f_1$ affine, and clause (2) makes $X_1$ affine because $S_1$ is affine. Clause (1) of [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] makes $f_1$ smooth of relative dimension one. Pulling back the inverse of $n$ on $S$ gives its inverse on $S_1$, and $n\Lambda=0$ is unchanged. The universal lower-degree properties also hold for $f_1$: compose any preliminary map $T\to S_1$ with $S_1\to S$ and apply the original hypothesis, as required by [sk-def-bc].

source.place: Tags 01SD (lemma-base-change-affine), 01S6 (definition-affine, source affine over affine target), 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth), 02NK (lemma-base-change-relative-dimension-d). Universal quantifiers from sk-def-bc.

proof.text: Apply [sk-lem-universal-datum] to $f_1$. Step 1 supplies fixed-base failure in degree $q$, step 2 supplies its universal lower-degree hypotheses and all geometric and coefficient hypotheses, and $r\le q-1$ is equivalent to $r<q$ for integer $r$. The lemma produces a base change $f':X'\to S'$ of $f_1$, an affine integral normal $S'=\operatorname{Spec}A$ whose fraction field $L$ is algebraically closed, an algebraically closed extension $K/L$ and its geometric generic point $g:\operatorname{Spec}K\to S'$, a Cartesian square with horizontal map $h:Y\to X'$ and vertical map $e:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}K$, and an integer $d\mid n$ invertible on $S'$ with $R^qh_*(\Lambda/d\Lambda)\ne0$.

source.place: Statement, arbitrary-ring universal datum; Stacks Tag 0F08, etale-cohomology.tex, lemma-base-change-does-not-hold, is the cyclic-coefficient source.

proof.text: The statement of [sk-lem-universal-datum] explicitly gives that $f'$ is affine and smooth of relative dimension one. Its base $S'$ is affine, so clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] makes $X'$ affine. The base $S'=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is integral and normal in the sense of [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois], so $A$ is a domain whose localizations $A_{\mathfrak p}$ are normal domains, i.e. $A$ is a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]; it is then a normal domain: if $x\in L=\operatorname{Frac}A$ is integral over $A$, then $x\in A_{\mathfrak m}$ for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, so the ideal $\{a\in A: ax\in A\}$ lies in no maximal ideal, hence equals $A$ and $x\in A$. Thus the square in step 3 satisfies every hypothesis of [sk-thm-vanishing]: the base is the spectrum of the normal domain $A$ with algebraically closed fraction field $L$, $K/L$ is an algebraically closed extension with the specified geometric generic map, the morphism and source are affine, and $d$ is invertible on $S'$. Applying that theorem at $q\ge1$ gives $R^qh_*(\Lambda/d\Lambda)=0$, contradicting step 3, in the same category of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules.

source.place: Statement, arbitrary-ring curve-test vanishing; Stacks Tag 0EYU, etale-cohomology.tex, theorem-smooth-base-change, second proof, final vanishing argument; Tag 01S6 for affine source over affine base.

proof.text: There can therefore be no base change $S_0\to S$ for which $\mathrm{BC}(f_0,\Lambda,q)$ fails. By [sk-def-bc] this is exactly $\mathrm{BC}(f,\Lambda,q)$ universally.

source.place: Final contradiction conclusion; universal quantifier as defined in sk-def-bc (Stacks Tag 0F02, etale-cohomology.tex, remark-base-change-holds).

split_report.summary: Five steps implement the contradiction, explicitly distinguishing universal failure from fixed-base failure. Reused the existing field-failure lemma to produce an affine base with a fixed counterexample, verified geometry by existing permanence nodes, applied the universal-datum statement with its exact fixed-base hypothesis, then contradicted its nonvanishing by the existing vanishing theorem. No new nodes, coefficient changes, or Lean attachments. Added definitions used in the statement. The older sbc induction is a related Z/n specialization, not the arbitrary-coefficient statement, so same_as is empty. Second reading explicitly checks that the field-valued witness is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, using two existing Mathlib leaves. Maintainer reading (Q55): step 4 now writes out why the integral normal affine base of the datum is the spectrum of a normal domain, as sk-thm-vanishing requires, citing the two definitions.
split_report.blueprint: Current blueprint sole contradiction paragraph: preliminary affine-base failure and inherited universal hypotheses (steps 1-2), applying sk-lem-universal-datum (step 3), affineness and sk-thm-vanishing contradiction (step 4), universal conclusion (step 5).

tool_uses.why: Produces precisely the affine preliminary failure required before the unit applies sk-lem-universal-datum, whose current statement requires a fixed-base failure and affine source. This is the already cited reduction lane (Tag 0F07) inside that datum lemma, not a replacement of the curve-test/vanishing route.

Supplies the generic base-change stability of smooth relative dimension one for the preliminary affine-base morphism. The unit route explicitly requires this stability but its definition nodes do not assert the theorem.
